findings.why: They crisply pin down the central disagreement: emergent counterfactuals from next-token scaling vs need for explicit causal modules.
findings.quote: We disagree on whether autoregressive next-token prediction can achieve robust out-of-distribution causal reasoning without an explicit, non-statistical world model.

findings.why: A claims corpora contain traces of real interventions, enabling causal learning; B replies that reading about interventions remains purely observational data.
findings.quote: Natural language corpora explicitly contain the trace of billions of interventions

findings.why: A claims autoregressive rollouts with a code interpreter perform real interventions (do-operations); B says it’s still just conditioning on new tokens, not genuine causal discovery by the model.
findings.quote: it executes a real-time intervention over an external causal graph.

findings.tag: In-context learning as dynamic weight updates
findings.why: A asserts activation states function as implicit weight updates enabling new causal states; B argues the model can’t synthesize orthogonal bases if the manifold compressed them.
findings.quote: in-context activation states functionally act as dynamic weight updates

findings.why: A treats residual entropy spikes as driving hypothesis branching; B argues residuals track token novelty, not world-uncertainty or causal validity.
findings.quote: Residual stream geometry tracks token predictability, not epistemic uncertainty about the world.

findings.tag: Does scale purge or entrench confounders?
findings.why: Direct clash: A says parsimony at scale filters spurious correlations; B counters that scaling entrenches human-wide confounders in the corpus.
findings.quote: Scale does not filter confounders; it weaponizes them.

judge.arc: Sustained, technical disagreement that deepens across multiple fronts (data type, inference-time behavior, representation geometry, and scaling), with no convergence.
